chapter: Chicago, Lee Collins and the road
title: White Sox Park with Uncle Paul and King Oliver; Black baseball
summary: Paul took Danny to a White Sox game with King Oliver, and Milt recalls the Colored Giants on 39th Street.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: The commuter trains coming. Well, that was my first taste of Chicago. Then they took us... My Uncle Paul taken us to the ballgame, the White Sox Park, which was on the South Side.

And I went there with him and King Oliver. They all were going to see some helluva game. I didn't know nothin' about no baseball. And we went there, and there were all these people. I'd never seen that many people. And we sat up in the top, and I hear him talking about Harry Hooper. Harry Hooper this, Harry Hooper that. He was a White ballplayer who was supposed to have been a sensation, a great center-fielder. Well, that was the music business, see...
Right on 35th Street there, right by the White Sox Park, past... Well, 39th Street was where the Black ballplayers had theirs, over in that same direction -- 39th
Street. The Giants. I can't think of their name.
He was the man. So he was a big man in Black baseball.
That was a great, great city. Great. Still is, I guess.
